Listen to this article Share …Kano facility to reduce gas transportation challenges, support expansion of retail outlets across the North The Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF) and Rolling Energy Limited have commissioned a 300,000-standard cubic metres daily liquefied-to-compressed natural gas (LCNG) facility in Kano State to supply CNG stations and accelerate the expansion of gas distribution infrastructure across northern Nigeria. The facility, located at Tamburawa in Dawakin Kudu Local Government Area, is designed to receive, store and regasify liquefied natural gas (LNG) before distributing it as compressed natural gas (CNG) to retail outlets, transport operators and other consumers. The investment is expected to address one of the major constraints to CNG adoption in northern Nigeria: the distance between gas supply sources and emerging markets, which has increased the logistical burden of delivering gas to filling stations. The facility was commissioned on Tuesday alongside a retail station at Tamburawa and an LCNG daughter station at Hotoro in Tarauni Local Government Area by the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo. The Hotoro station has a capacity of 21,000 standard cubic metres daily, while the combined facilities are expected to serve up to 2,500 cars and tricycles and 200 trucks daily. Mubarak Danbatta, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Rolling Energy, said the Tamburawa hub would provide a strategic supply point for investors seeking to establish CNG stations in Kano, Jigawa, Zaria and other parts of northern Nigeria. He explained that operators would no longer need to depend entirely on transporting gas from distant supply locations such as Ajaokuta and Obajana in Kogi State. According to him, the investment is structured to support other businesses and investors, rather than function exclusively as a supply facility for Rolling Energy’s retail outlets. “We are not building stations only for our own customers. We are creating infrastructure that enables other businesses to serve their own customers and grow,” Danbatta said. He added that the facilities also incorporate vehicle conversion workshops equipped with Greco CNG kits, with Tamburawa capable of converting 20 vehicles daily and Hotoro six. Executive Director of MDGIF, Oluwole Adama, said the Kano project was part of an 18-facility partnership with Rolling Energy covering three states and the Federal Capital Territory. He said the infrastructure could collectively refuel up to 2,500 cars and tricycles and 200 trucks daily, providing transport operators with an alternative to increasingly expensive petrol. Adama said petrol currently sells for about N1,420 per litre in Kano, while the equivalent energy from CNG costs approximately N600. He estimated that a tricycle operator spending N14,200 daily on 10 litres of petrol could reduce the expenditure to N6,000 by switching to CNG, saving N8,200 daily. Beyond transportation, he said improved access to gas could reduce logistics costs for businesses moving agricultural produce, livestock and manufactured goods across the region. The MDGIF executive said the fund, established under Section 52 of the Petroleum Industry Act, was designed to address infrastructure gaps in the midstream and downstream gas sectors through partnerships with private investors. Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekpo, described the commissioning as a demonstration of the Federal Government’s commitment to converting its gas policies into infrastructure under the Renewed Hope Agenda. “What we commission today is more than three pieces of infrastructure. It is Renewed Hope made tangible,” he said. Danbatta also disclosed that the partnership with MDGIF covered plans for regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) gas-to-power facilities to support industrial operations. He said Kaduna and Borno states would be the next focus of expansion, with three facilities planned in each state, while Jigawa, Katsina, Sokoto and Zamfara were also being considered. The planned expansion is expected to create a wider network of gas supply and distribution infrastructure, with Tamburawa potentially serving as a major supply hub for additional CNG stations across the North. The Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, was represented at the event by the Commissioner for Power and Renewable Energy, Gaddafi Sani Shehu. Also present was Professor Umar Garba Danbatta, President of the Nigerian Academy of Engineering, alongside representatives of the Presidential Initiative on CNG and Electric Vehicles, regulators, community leaders and industry stakeholders. Ifeoma Okeke-Korieocha Ifeoma Okeke-Korieocha is the Aviation Correspondent at BusinessDay Media Limited, publishers of BusinessDay Newspapers. She is also the Deputy Editor, BusinessDay Weekender Magazine, the Saturday Weekend edition of BusinessDay. She holds a BSC in Mass Communication from the prestigious University of Nigeria, Nsukka and a Masters degree in Marketing at the University of Lagos. As the lead writer on the aviation desk, Ifeoma is responsible and in charge of the three weekly aviation and travel pages in BusinessDay and BDSunday. She also overseas and edits all pages of BusinessDay Saturday Weekender. She has written various investigative, features and news stories in aviation and business related issues and has been severally nominated for award in the category of Aviation Writer of the Year by the Nigeria Media Nite-Out awards; one of the Nigeria’s most prestigious media awards ceremonies. Ifeoma is a one-time winner of the prestigious Nigeria Media Merit Award under the 'Aviation Writer of the Year' Category. She is the 2025 Eloy Award winner under the Print Media Journalist category. She has undergone several journalism trainings by various prestigious organisations. Ifeoma is also a fellow of the Female Reporters Leadership Fellowship of the Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism.
